Member (Gurpreet Chen): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Gurpreet Chen, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Chen): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Chen): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Chen): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Gurpreet Chen): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Gurpreet Chen): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Gurpreet Chen): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Gurpreet Chen): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Gurpreet Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Gurpreet Chen): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Gurpreet Chen): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Gurpreet Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Lucas Campbell): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Lucas Campbell, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Campbell): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Campbell): Yes, that's right.
Member (Lucas Campbell): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Lucas Campbell): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Lucas Campbell): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Lucas Campbell): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000332.transcript:
Member (Arjun O'Brien): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Arjun O'Brien, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun O'Brien): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Arjun O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Arjun O'Brien): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Arjun O'Brien): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Arjun O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Arjun O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Arjun O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Arjun O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Arjun O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Cote): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Owen Cote, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Cote): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Cote): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Owen Cote): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Owen Cote): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Owen Cote): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Owen Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Owen Cote): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Owen Cote): Great, that helps.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Owen Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Morrison): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Owen Morrison, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Morrison): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Owen Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Owen Morrison): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Owen Morrison): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Owen Morrison): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Owen Morrison): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Owen Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Owen Morrison): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Owen Morrison): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Owen Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Patel): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Leila Patel, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Patel): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Leila Patel): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Leila Patel): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Leila Patel): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Leila Patel): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Leila Patel): They said they called and got the same answer as me.

Member (Leila Patel): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Leila Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Leila Patel): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Leila Patel): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Leila Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Morrison): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Where is the money going?

Member (Mei Morrison): Who follows up?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Mei Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Fortin): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.

Member (Hannah Fortin): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Lavoie): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Arjun Lavoie): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.

Member (Liam Roy): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Liam Roy): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Liam Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Liam Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Liam Roy): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Liam Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Martin): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Arjun Martin): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Arjun Martin): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Arjun Martin): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.

Member (Arjun Martin): So is this actually getting fixed today?

Member (Arjun Martin): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Arjun Martin): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Arjun Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Olivia Morrison): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Olivia Morrison, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.

Member (Olivia Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Olivia Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Olivia Morrison): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Olivia Morrison): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Olivia Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Olivia Morrison): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Olivia Morrison): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Olivia Morrison): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Olivia Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Olivia Singh): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Olivia Singh, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Singh): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Singh): Yes, that's right.
Member (Olivia Singh): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Olivia Singh): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Olivia Singh): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Olivia Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Olivia Singh): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Olivia Singh): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Olivia Singh): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Olivia Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Owen Morrison): I was approved for this weeks ago and I still haven't been reimbursed.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): No, all future claims will go to the new one.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the new account is on file and the 120-dollar payment is reissued. You'll see it within three business days.
Member (Owen Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Yes. I've updated the account and reissued the payment, so it should land within three business days.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): No, all future claims will go to the new one.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So the new account is on file and the 120-dollar payment is reissued. You'll see it within three business days.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-002097.transcript:
Member (Olivia Chen): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Olivia Chen, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Chen): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Olivia Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Olivia Chen): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Olivia Chen): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Olivia Chen): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Olivia Chen): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Olivia Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Olivia Chen): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Olivia Chen): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Olivia Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Patel): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.

Member (Arjun Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Patel): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Arjun Patel): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Arjun Patel): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Arjun Patel): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.

Member (Arjun Patel): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.

Member (Arjun Patel): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Arjun Patel): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Arjun Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Kim): I'm following up again — my dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Owen Kim, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Kim): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Owen Kim): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Kim): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Owen Kim): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Owen Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Owen Kim): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Owen Kim): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Owen Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-002708.transcript:
Member (Mei Martin): I'm following up again — I cancelled my life insurance before it renewed and you still took the payment.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Mei Martin, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Martin): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Mei Martin): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Martin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Martin): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which policy is this about?
Member (Mei Martin): My term life policy. It renewed this month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did you get a confirmation of the cancellation?
Member (Mei Martin): No, I was told it would be processed.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): If the cost came down, would you want to keep some coverage?
Member (Mei Martin): Maybe, if it's affordable.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the policy billing history and the forms received.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I can see your call from the 17th and the renewal payment taken on the 1st.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The renewal rate is higher because the policy moved into a new age band on renewal.
Member (Mei Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The premium increase follows the renewal schedule in your policy, so I can't change the rate. I can send you the renewal notice and your options, including reducing the coverage amount.
Member (Mei Martin): Nobody told me it would triple.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The notice went out 60 days before renewal, but I understand it's a shock at that size.
Member (Mei Martin): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.
Member (Mei Martin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Hannah Ahmed): I'm following up again — my pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Hannah Ahmed, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Ahmed): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Hannah Ahmed): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Hannah Ahmed): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Hannah Ahmed): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): Who follows up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Hannah Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.
